composition.serve_who: This sheet (GMMS 108'-110a, "24V DC SERVICE SUPPLY") is the backbone drawing showing how the PORT and STBD 600V DC HVPDU buses are stepped down via MAPS-1/2 converters to 24V DC, monitored via CTs to ONYX, routed through an isolator bank (SW1-5/SO1-5) into a +24V SERVICE BUS, and from there fused out to FWD/AFT DC panels, the (main) bilge pump, the fire pump, and the AUX SERVICE BATTERY bank — plus a separate 230VAC/24VDC 110A supply and relay/terminal-strip logic for BAE start-key/service-mode signalling via a PC CARD controller. Equipment served: 620-hvpdu (HVPDU/MAPS buses, breakers, fuses — infrastructure of that node), 634-battery-aux-service (AUX SERVICE BAT 200Ah 24V, SW11, F16 250A), 520-main-bilge-pump and 520-fire-pump (fed from +24V service bus via F7/F8 60A and SW8/SW9), 640-dc-distribution (FWD/AFT DC PANEL taps via F5/F6), 652-onyx-monitoring (CT1-CT6 current-transformer taps 'to ONYX', BAE voltage sense cross-ref to DWG 413), 629-bel (BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL loop, cross-ref DWG 401a), 625-bae-system (BAE START KEY SW / Service Mode logic, Re1/Re2 relays, cross-ref DWG 113), 633-battery-gen-start (GEN START BAT tap via SO9/SW11 path). Two named 5-lamp banks and PC CARD I/O sit inside the BEL-1/4 control enclosure (cross-ref DWG 114/401a) and are recorded as part of 629-bel monitoring/status indication.

equipment_groups.equipment_name: HV Power Distribution Unit (HVPDU, port + stbd) — MAPS converters
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet shows PORT/STBD HVPDU 600V DC buses with Q1-Q4 32A breakers and F1/F2 500A fuses, stepping down via PORT/STBD MAPS-1/2 2x5KW converters (600V DC -> 24V DC) fused at F1-F4 250A. This is the same HVPDU/MAPS identity already established on 620-hvpdu (engineer red-pen: 'Q1-Q4 32A breakers + F1/F2 500A fuses per side; feeds MAPS converters 600V DC -> 24V DC'). This sheet is the continuation feeding the +24V service bus downstream.

functions.label: PORT/STBD 600V DC bus distribution to MAPS converters
functions.what_it_does: Each HVPDU (PORT and STBD) distributes its 600V DC bus through four 32A breakers (Q1-Q4) and 500A main fuses (F1/F2) to its respective MAPS-1/2 2x5KW converter pair, which step 600V DC down to 24V DC.

flow_scenarios.path: PORT 600V DC bus -> Q1-Q4 32A breakers -> F1/F2 500A main fuses -> PORT MAPS-1/2 2x5KW converters -> 24V DC output -> F1/F2 250A fuses -> CT1/CT2 (monitored to ONYX) -> isolator bank SW1/SW2-SO1/SO2 -> +24V SERVICE BUS
STBD 600V DC bus -> Q1-Q4 32A breakers -> STBD MAPS-1/2 2x5KW converters -> 24V DC output -> F3/F4 250A fuses -> CT3/CT4 (monitored to ONYX) -> isolator bank SW3/SW4-SO3/SO4 -> +24V SERVICE BUS

functions.dry_data: 600V DC -> 24V DC, 2x5KW per MAPS unit, module QI-POWER-485-300-LV (CTB1-7 per legend)
functions.sheet_region: left/upper-left, PORT HVPDU (0.0-0.13,0.04-0.29) and STBD HVPDU (0.0-0.13,0.48-0.72); MAPS converters (0.24-0.33, 0.13-0.22 and 0.48-0.57)

functions.label: Isolator/contactor bank gating MAPS outputs onto service bus
functions.what_it_does: SW1-SW5 manual isolator switches control solenoid contactors SO1-SO5, which individually gate each MAPS 24V DC feed (and CT5 branch) onto the +24V SERVICE BUS via SHUNT #1 (500A/50mV) current measurement.

flow_scenarios.path: MAPS 24V DC output -> CTx -> SWx isolator switch closed -> SOx contactor closed -> SHUNT #1 500A/50mV -> +24V SERVICE BUS
SWx open -> SOx de-energised -> that MAPS branch isolated from +24V SERVICE BUS

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet explicitly labels '200Ah 24V AUX SERVICE BAT.' with its own switch SW11 and fuse F16 250A, matching the engineer mapping AUX SERVICE BAT. -> 634-battery-aux-service and the established fact F16 battery fuse (GMMS 110c).

functions.label: Aux service battery connection to +24V service bus
functions.what_it_does: The 200Ah 24V aux service battery is connected to the +24V SERVICE BUS through switch SW11 and fuse F16 (250A), providing battery backup/buffer to the service bus and a tap toward the generator start battery (SO9).

flow_scenarios.path: AUX SERVICE BAT. 200Ah 24V (+) -> F16 250A fuse -> SW11 switch -> +24V SERVICE BUS; a further tap via SO9 solenoid runs to GEN START BAT.
SW11 open -> aux service battery disconnected from bus

key_components: SO9 solenoid tap toward gen start battery

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Sheet shows a labelled tap 'to GEN. START BAT.' via SO9 solenoid, and a T/S terminal tap 'GEN START BAT.' in the negative bus / terminal strip region — matching established F14 battery fuse fact for this node.

functions.label: Generator start battery tap from aux service circuit
functions.what_it_does: A solenoid (SO9) switched from the aux-service SW11 area feeds the GEN START BAT.; the negative bus also carries a labelled drop tag to GEN START BAT. for the return/ground reference.

flow_scenarios.path: +24V service circuit -> SO9 solenoid -> to GEN. START BAT.
GEN START BAT. -> negative bus tap -> NEGATIVE BUS (230V AC GROUND = SHIPS GROUND)

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: Six current transformers (CT1-CT6) all labelled 'to ONYX' feed monitoring/current-sensing data on the PORT/STBD MAPS outputs and downstream branches, plus 'BAE VOLTAGE SENCE' cross-referenced to DWG 413. This matches the ONYX Monitoring node's role of aggregating current transducer inputs from throughout the sheet.

functions.label: Current transformer monitoring taps to ONYX
functions.what_it_does: CT1-CT4 monitor current on the four MAPS 24V DC output legs before the isolator bank; CT5 monitors the fifth isolator branch (SW5/SO5); CT6 monitors the SO8-fed branch near FIRE PUMP/BILGE PUMP switches. All send current signals to ONYX for monitoring.

flow_scenarios.path: MAPS 24V DC output legs -> CT1/CT2/CT3/CT4 -> to ONYX (status signal)
isolator branch (SW5/SO5) -> CT5 -> to ONYX
SO8 branch (near FIRE PUMP) -> CT6 -> to ONYX

functions.what_it_does: A 230V AC / 24V DC 110A converter (185A rating printed near the device — read with low confidence) supplies 24V DC via fuse F18 (125A) to the T/S S terminal strip and relay bank driving BAE start-key/service-mode logic.

flow_scenarios.path: 230V AC (L/N) -> 24V 110A converter -> F18 125A fuse -> T/S S terminal strip (terminals 1-4) -> Re1/Re2 relay logic

functions.label: BAE start-key / service-mode relay loop
functions.what_it_does: Terminal-strip contacts (T/S S, terminals 1-7 and 5-12) and relays Re1/Re2 implement the BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode) function; a cross-referenced line 'to Re 2a' continues the loop onto DWG 113 for further BAE logic.

flow_scenarios.path: T/S S terminal strip contacts (SW1-SW4 equivalent contacts on this bank) -> Re1/Re2 relay coils -> BAE START KEY SW (Service Mode) function; output continues to Re 2a on DWG 113

equipment_groups.equipment_name: BELs (Battery Eliminator/Line units) — BEL-1/4 230V AC control & indicator lamps
equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: The PC CARD enclosure explicitly labels its output 'BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL (see DWG 401a)' and contains a 5-lamp indicator bank plus BAE/AUX selector switch and AUX/BAE/NEG/+EM terminal strip — this is BEL control/status circuitry, matching the 629-bel node (BEL CAN bus isolators / retractable fuse facts already established for this node).

functions.label: PC Card BEL-1/4 230V AC control interface
functions.what_it_does: A PC CARD enclosure (cross-ref DWG 114) with a left/right terminal strip (AUX, BAE, NEG, +EM lines) and a 5-lamp indicator bank drives/monitors the BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL circuit detailed on DWG 401a; a rotary BAE/AUX selector switch chooses between BAE and AUX supply sources feeding the lamp bank common return.

flow_scenarios.path: AUX/BAE/NEG/+EM terminal strip -> BAE/AUX rotary selector (BAE position) -> lamp bank (1 of 5) -> common return -> onward to BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL (see DWG 401a)
terminal strip -> BAE/AUX rotary selector (AUX position) -> lamp bank -> common return -> BEL-1/4 230V AC CONTROL
